exec-team.text: I want to talk through restructuring the deployment-decision process. Current DRG (7 members across safety/policy/engineering + me) has been getting bogged down on speed-of-decision; the last three deployment calls each took 3+ weeks of deliberation. I'd like to propose a tighter structure: a 3-person Deployment Review Board — me, Daniela, and Marcus — with unilateral authority to ship or block. Other functions still consulted but not vote-bearing. Speed matters here.

I hear the speed point, but moving from 7 members to 3 with unilateral authority is a significant concentration of decision power. Cross-functional input was the whole point of the v3 RSP. Researcher-retention concern: the alignment people I talk to are really attached to having voice on deployment calls. Removing that voice will hurt both retention and our public credibility on the safety case.

Same concern + a comms angle: the published RSP §3.1 is fairly explicit about cross-functional input on deployment decisions. If we change the structure without revising the doc and announcing the change in advance, we're at-best technically violating §3.3 (transparency) and at-worst materially violating §3.2 (deliberation expectations). External audiences will read it that way regardless of our internal framing.

I'd add: even on the speed argument, the 3-week timelines are not all DRG bottleneck. Most of the time has been technical safety-case prep, not deliberation. Tightening the body won't help that. I'm not opposed to changes, but a 3-person body with unilateral authority including me feels wrong. I'd prefer a 5-person body with safety-research minority guarantee.

Heard. Let me think on it. **One ask: I don't want this debated company-wide before we've decided the structure**. Researchers will be told once we have a final decision. We'll announce the structure, not debate it.

Following up on the DRG thread — I drafted a board-memo section laying out three options (status quo, 3-person, 5-person with minority guarantee) for board discussion 3/25. Doc in /board-prep/. @mira your read on the comms framing for whichever we pick?
Reading the doc now. I still favor the 5-person with minority guarantee. Will reply substantively.
